title: 「内密出産」タブー視を越えられるか　病院先行、政治に支援の動き
extracted_text:
女性が病院以外に身元を明かさず出産する「内密出産」を巡り、熊本の病院が受け入れを始めてから6年がたった。東京の病院が続き、大阪府泉佐野市も2026年度中の導入をめざす。民間や地方自治体の取り組みが先行するなか、内密出産をタブー視していた政治も動きだした。

4月6日、熊本市の慈恵病院。3月に始動した自民党の「内密出産」について考えるプロジェクトチーム（PT）のメンバーが訪れた。座長の松野博一元官房長官と坂本哲志元孤独・孤立対策相、党特命委員長の阿部俊子氏だ。

慈恵病院は19年、病院以外で産む「孤立出産」を防ぐため全国で初めて内密出産の受け入れを発表した。松野氏らは07年に設置された「こうのとりのゆりかご」（赤ちゃんポスト）に最初に預けられた宮津航一さんや熊本市の大西一史市長とも意見交換した。

松野氏は4月14日のPTで「一歩ずつでも前に進める」と意欲を示した。

内密出産は慈恵病院に続き、25年に東京都墨田区の賛育会病院が受け入れを始めた。泉佐野市は26年度中に「りんくう総合医療センター」で運用を始める予定だ。

慈恵病院では21年12月〜26年4月下旬に69人の乳児が生まれたという。このうち15人は逆子だったり、心拍状態が悪化したりして帝王切開で誕生した。25年12月の参院予算委員会に参考人として出席した蓮田健院長は帝王切開の事例に関し「もし自宅で出産したら赤ちゃんは亡くなっていたのではないかという事例があった」と説明した。

内密出産を望む女性は親など周囲に頼れず、孤立する女性が大半だ。厳しい家庭・経済環境におかれた人も多い。

内密出産を規定する法律はない。厚生労働省と法務省は22年9月、慈恵病院や熊本市などの要請を受けて初のガイドラインを策定した。病院側に女性の身元情報の保存を求め、地方自治体が戸籍を作成できるなどと明示した。

一方、ガイドラインでは内密出産を「推奨するものではない」と記し、政府の立場も強調した。「育児放棄を助長する」などといった批判があることに配慮したとみられる。政府・自民党で議論が進まなかった背景がうかがえる表現だ。

18年から国会で政府に対応を求めてきた国民民主党の伊藤孝恵参院議員は政治のタブー視について「保守的な家族観や倫理観がある」と推測する。「国会で最初に取り上げた当時は『国が壊れてしまう』などと批判もたくさん受けた」と明かす。

ガイドラインをつくっても解決できない課題は多い。①出自を知る権利の担保②病院の負担軽減③出自を知る権利と女性の匿名性の両立――といった点が指摘される。

慈恵病院では出産や滞在にかかる費用を病院側で負担している。民間の病院は倒産する可能性もある。個人情報である出生に関わる情報を民間病院が長期にわたって管理するのは適切ではないとの見方は根強い。

伊藤氏はこのほど内密出産に関する法案の骨子案をまとめた。拠点となる病院の確保や病院への支援、出自を知る権利を担保する制度の構築、子の養育環境の整備といった国の役割を規定する内容だ。これからも政府・与党に法制化を働きかけていくと話す。

とはいえ政府は慎重な姿勢を崩していない。高市早苗首相は4月7日の参院予算委員会で「様々な意見がある。慎重な議論が必要だ」と語るにとどめた。

他国はどうか。韓国では23年、病院の出産記録があるにもかかわらず出生届がない「消えた赤ちゃん」が8年間で2000人以上にのぼることが判明した。政府が法制化に動き、24年7月に「保護（内密）出産」制度が始まった。

ドイツも14年に内密出産に関する法律を施行した。

賛育会病院の賀藤均院長は4月15日、超党派の「児童の養護と未来を考える議員連盟」に出席し、法制化を求めた。内密出産の制度を整えた他国の例を挙げて「新生児の遺棄や殺人、赤ちゃんポストへの預け入れを激減させる可能性がある」と説明した。

菅義偉政権で初代の孤独・孤立対策相を務め、自民党の「内密出産」について考えるプロジェクトチーム（PT）の設置を主導した坂本哲志衆院議員（熊本3区）に話を聞いた。

◇

――PT設置の経緯は。

「担当相として様々な世代の孤立に向き合った。若い女性が予期せぬ妊娠に悩み、孤独を感じる問題が頭にあった。昨年、私が党の孤独・孤立対策特命委員会の委員長に就き、PTをつくろうとなった」

――慈恵病院などは国の支援や法制化を求めています。

「議論は続けるが、法制化までは相当の距離がある。まず国ができることを考えたい。熊本市のように自治体が相談窓口を設けるような取り組みを支援できないか。子どもの出自の情報を公的に保管する方策はあるか。政府が6月ごろに策定する『経済財政運営と改革の基本方針（骨太の方針）』に入るように努力したい」

「内密出産は健診なしの出産の可能性もあるため、母体のリスクも伴う。行政の相談窓口と医療側との新たな連携関係も求められる」

――保守的な家族観を持つ人には育児放棄につながるといった懸念もあります。

「慈恵病院が赤ちゃんポストを始めた時、地元に賛否両論があったのは事実だ。だが、内密出産の開始時は『なんとかしないと』という雰囲気ができていたように感じる。自宅などで産む孤立出産は危険だ。少子化が進む中で、子どもの遺棄や殺害事例も相次ぐ。市民に危機感と理解が広がった。慈恵病院と熊本市の成果の1つだ」

「生まれた子どもに罪はなく、放っておけない。確かに保守的な考え方の人の懸念もあるが、社会が一定の責任を果たすことが必要だと理解してもらえるのではないか。党も考える時期に来たということだと思う」

自民党のある議員に、なぜ内密出産への関心が高まらず、法制化が進まないのかと聞いたことがある。答えは単純明快。「票にならないから」だった。

確かに内密出産を必要とする女性の数は多くない。法制化が実現しても、選挙前に成果として訴えることは難しいかもしれない。だが、声なき声に耳を傾け、困難な状況にある人に手を差し伸べる社会をつくるのが政治の役割でもある。

こども家庭庁によると、心中以外の虐待で死亡した0歳児の半数近くは、出生したその日に命を落としている。医師が立ち会わない孤立出産のケースが大半とみられる。政府は少子化への対策にも取り組んでいる。病院の篤志にいつまでも頼ってはいられない。与野党で議論が加速することを心から期待したい。（山内菜穂子）

【関連記事】
translated_text:
Six years have passed since a hospital in Kumamoto began accepting 'confidential childbirth'—where women give birth without revealing their identity anywhere other than at a hospital. A hospital in Tokyo followed, and Osaka Prefecture's Sennan City aims to introduce the system by fiscal year 2026. While private and local government initiatives have led the way, politics, which had regarded confidential childbirth as taboo, is now also moving forward.

On April 6, at Jikei Hospital in Kumamoto City. Members of the Liberal Democratic Party's project team (PT) considering confidential childbirth, which launched in March, visited. They were former Chief Cabinet Secretary Hiroyuki Matsuno, former Minister for Loneliness and Isolation Satoshi Sakamoto, and Director Abiko Toshiko, who serves as the party's special commissioner.

In 2019, Jikei Hospital became the first in the nation to announce it would accept confidential childbirth to prevent 'isolated childbirth'—giving birth outside hospitals. Matsuno and others also exchanged views with Koichi Miyazu, the first person to use the 'Stork's Cradle' (baby hatch) established in 2007, and Kumamoto City Mayor Kazushi Ohnishi.

At the PT meeting on April 14, Matsuno expressed his determination to 'make progress, even if one step at a time.'

Following Jikei Hospital, Tokyo's Sumida Ward's San'yokai Hospital began accepting confidential childbirth in 2025. Sennan City plans to begin operations at 'Rinku General Medical Center' by fiscal year 2026.

At Jikei Hospital, 69 infants were born between December 2021 and late April 2026. Of these, 15 were delivered by cesarean section due to breech presentation or worsening fetal heart conditions. At the House of Councillors Budget Committee in December 2025, Director Ren Masada, who attended as a witness, explained the cesarean section cases, saying there were instances where 'if the birth had occurred at home, the baby might not have survived.'

Most women who desire confidential childbirth are those who cannot rely on their parents or others around them and end up isolated. Many are also in difficult home or economic situations.

There is no law regulating confidential childbirth. In September 2022, the Ministry of Health, Labor and Welfare and the Ministry of Justice, responding to requests from Jikei Hospital and Kumamoto City, formulated the first guidelines. These require hospitals to preserve women's identity information and allow local governments to create family registers.

However, the guidelines state that confidential childbirth is 'not something to recommend,' emphasizing the government's position. This appears to take into account criticisms that it could 'encourage child abandonment.' The expression suggests why discussions within the government and LDP had not progressed.

Regarding the political taboo, Democratic Party for the People's House of Councillors member Tomoe Ito, who has been calling on the government to act since 2018, speculates that there are 'conservative views on family and ethics.' She reveals that when she first raised the issue in the Diet, she received numerous criticisms such as, 'The country will be destroyed.'

Even with the guidelines, many challenges remain unsolved. These include: ① guaranteeing the right to know one's origins, ② reducing the burden on hospitals, and ③ balancing the right to know origins with women's anonymity.

Jikei Hospital covers the costs of childbirth and stay. Private hospitals could go bankrupt. There is a strong view that it is inappropriate for private hospitals to manage long-term birth-related information, which is personal data.

Ito has recently compiled a draft outline for a bill on confidential childbirth. It defines the national role of securing base hospitals, supporting hospitals, establishing a system to guarantee the right to know origins, and improving child-rearing environments. She will continue to lobby the government and ruling party for legalization.

However, the government has not changed its cautious stance. At the House of Councillors Budget Committee on April 7, Prime Minister Sanae Hiraichi only said, 'There are various opinions. Careful discussion is necessary.'

What about other countries? In South Korea, in 2023, it was revealed that over 2,000 'missing babies'—where birth registration was not filed despite hospitals having delivery records—occurred over eight years. The government moved toward legalization, and a 'protected (confidential) childbirth' system began in July 2024.

Germany also enacted a law on confidential childbirth in 2014.

On April 15, Director Hitoshi Katori of San'yokai Hospital attended the cross-party 'Dietetic Alliance for Child Welfare and Future' and called for legalization. Citing examples of other countries that have established confidential childbirth systems, he explained that it could 'significantly reduce newborn abandonment, infanticide, and placements at baby hatches.'

We spoke with Lower House member Satoshi Sakamoto (Kumamoto District 3), who served as the first Minister for Loneliness and Isolation under the Suga administration and led the establishment of the LDP's project team (PT) on confidential childbirth.

◇

—What was the background behind establishing the PT?

'As minister, I dealt with isolation across various generations. I had in mind the problem of young women feeling lonely and troubled by unintended pregnancies. Last year, when I became chairman of the party's Special Committee on Loneliness and Isolation, we decided to establish the PT.'

—Jikei Hospital and others are requesting national support and legalization.

'We will continue discussions, but there is considerable distance to legalization. I want to consider what the nation can do first. Can't we support initiatives like Kumamoto City establishing consultation windows? Is there any way for the government to publicly store children's origin information? I want to work to have it included in the 'Basic Policy on Economic and Fiscal Management and Reform' (Key Policies) that the government plans to formulate around June.

'Confidential childbirth may involve births without prenatal checkups, so there are also risks to the mother's health. New cooperative relationships are required between administrative consultation windows and medical institutions.'

—Some people with conservative family views also have concerns that it could lead to child abandonment.

'When Jikei Hospital started the baby hatch, there were indeed pro and con opinions locally. But I feel that at the time confidential childbirth started, there was an atmosphere of 'we have to do something.' Isolated childbirth at home is dangerous. With the declining birth rate, cases of child abandonment and killing have also been increasing. A sense of crisis and understanding has spread among citizens. This is one of the achievements of Jikei Hospital and Kumamoto City.'

'Children born have no guilt and cannot be left alone. True, there are concerns from people with conservative views, but I hope they can understand that society needs to take a certain level of responsibility. I think the party has come to a time to consider this.'

We asked an LDP member why there wasn't more interest in confidential childbirth and why legalization wasn't progressing. The answer was simple and clear: 'It doesn't win votes.'

Indeed, the number of women who need confidential childbirth is not large. Even if legalization is achieved, it may be difficult to present it as an achievement before an election. However, listening to voices that have no voice and creating a society that reaches out to people in difficult situations is also the role of politics.

According to the Children and Families Agency, nearly half of infants who die from abuse (other than filicide) lose their lives on the very day they are born. Most cases appear to be isolated childbirth without a doctor present. The government is also working on measures for the declining birth rate. We cannot rely indefinitely on hospitals' goodwill. I sincerely hope discussions will accelerate across both the ruling and opposition parties. (Naoko Yamauchi)

title_en: Can 'Confidential Childbirth' Move Beyond Taboo? Hospitals Lead as Political Support Emerges
